images.title: Neighbouring sides match
images.purpose: Show that all sides of a square are equal, so one known side fixes its neighbour.
images.composition: One big square centred, with two tick-marked sides and the two matching labels; wide white margins.
images.exact_structure: One square PQRS, outline teal #0072B2, sides exactly equal. Bottom side PQ labelled 6 cm. Left side PS highlighted reddish purple #CC79A7 and labelled 6 cm. PQ and PS each carry one identical tick mark. Right-angle mark at P. Exactly 1 square, 2 labelled sides, 2 tick marks.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a tick mark on only one of the two marked sides
images.takeaway: All sides of a square are equal.
images.description: Square PQRS with PQ and PS both marked 6 cm and carrying the same tick mark.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at PQ, then at PS, and say why PS needs no ruler.

image_decisions.why: One clean geometry picture carries the single idea of this video.
